mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the permission matrix definition allows Alloy to invent arbitrary permission combinations, violating the least-privilege invariant. The mutation tests whether LeastPrivilege and OwnershipBasedAccess genuinely depend on explicit matrix definition.

Removing the immutability constraint allows Alloy to create two distinct audit entries for the same task at the same time, violating the append-only property that the audit trail can be mutated. This tests whether the assertion genuinely checks for unmodifiable history.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj a1, a2: AuditEntry | a1.taskId = a2.taskId and a1.occurredAt = a2.occurredAt }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the ownership-based access constraint allows non-owners who are members (but not admins) to edit or delete tasks, violating the permission boundary. This tests whether the predicate actually enforces the FR-008/009/010 rules.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnershipViolation { some t: Task, tm: TeamMembership | tm.team = t.team and tm.role = Member and tm.user != t.owner and tm.user in editableBy[t] }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the cross-team isolation constraint allows users to view or access tasks outside their team, violating multi-tenant security. This tests whether the assertion genuinely enforces the byte-equivalent 404 invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_InformationLeakage { some t: Task, u: User | (no tm: TeamMembership | tm.user = u and tm.team = t.team) and u in viewableBy[t] }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the requirement that every task has a created audit entry allows tasks without audit trails, violating the immutable event log. This tests whether the assertion catches missing audit entries.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MissingAudit { some t: Task | no a: AuditEntry | a.task = t and a.changeType = Created }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the uniqueness constraint allows a task to have multiple owners, violating the single-owner invariant. This tests whether the assertion enforces one-to-one ownership.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MultipleOwners { some disj u1, u2: User, t: Task | t.owner = u1 and t.owner = u2 }
